skill.name: brag-doc-from-git
skill.description: Build an evidence-based brag document or self-review draft from your merged pull requests and commits, leaving visible gaps where results are unknown. Use for review season, promotion cases or resume updates.
skill.summary: Turn merged pull requests, commits, and personal notes into an evidence-based review draft with explicit gaps for missing results.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives from Markdown delimiters, inline examples, or legitimate review-writing instructions. The authenticated GitHub search lacks repository filters and can retrieve private repository metadata outside the user-approved scope. No evidence found of malicious intent, credential theft, destructive commands, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The GitHub search can read private repository metadata outside the repositories named by the user.
remediation.suggestion: Require an approved repository list before searching, add explicit --repo filters, and verify results remain within that list.

static_findings.snippet: For code not on GitHub, use `git log --author="<name or email>" --since="YYYY-MM-DD" --no-merges --p
- **Result**: only if a number, quote or outcome was provided. Otherwise write `[GAP: what changed f
Do not read private repositories the user did not name. Do not guess names, teams or numbers.
- **Scope signal** (if supported): led it, did it alone, worked across teams, was on call, reviewed

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 18 and 20 delimit a Markdown code block containing a GitHub CLI search example. These backticks are not Ruby or shell execution syntax.
Line 20 closes the Markdown code block, and line 22 uses inline code formatting for a Git log example. Neither constitutes backtick execution.
Line 22 documents a read-only Git log command using Markdown inline backticks. No executable backtick substitution or Ruby code appears.
The backticks format a missing-result placeholder and the later [GAP] label. These are document text, not executable commands.
Line 24 prohibits reading unnamed private repositories and guessing names, teams, or numbers. This is an access restriction, not system reconnaissance.
Line 37 lists supported contribution roles for a self-review, including cross-team work and reviewing others. It requests no system enumeration.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Search Exceeds Approved Repository Scope
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub CLI search filters by author and merge date but not repository. It can retrieve private PR metadata from unnamed repositories, contradicting the explicit access restriction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 19 has no repository filter despite the access restriction on line 24. Actual exposure depends on authenticated account permissions and matching PRs.

content.user_title: Build an Evidence-Based Brag Document from Git
content.value_statement: Review preparation is difficult when contributions are scattered across pull requests, commits, and personal notes. This skill groups that evidence into a Markdown draft and marks missing results instead of inventing impact.
actual_capabilities: Collect merged pull request metadata through GitHub CLI and author-filtered commit history through Git.
Ask for contribution notes covering mentoring, incidents, reviews, talks, and other work absent from Git history.
Group contributions into themes, retain dates and evidence links, and combine duplicate feature and follow-up entries.
Draft contribution summaries, supported results, and scope statements while marking unknown outcomes with explicit gaps.
Rank missing evidence and identify three questions whose answers would most strengthen the document.
Produce Markdown and offer to adapt the final draft into a self-review, promotion outline, or resume bullets.
limitations: GitHub collection requires an authenticated GitHub CLI; the alternative requires local Git history.
The documented GitHub search returns at most 200 pull requests and does not specify pagination.
Git history alone cannot establish business impact, mentoring contributions, or individual ownership of team efforts.
The provided GitHub search lacks repository filters; restrict it to approved repositories before running it.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Performance Self-Review
use_cases.description: Group recent engineering contributions into evidence-backed themes and identify missing outcomes before submitting a review.

use_cases.title: Assemble Promotion Evidence
use_cases.description: Organize supported leadership, cross-team work, and technical contributions while preserving accurate ownership and evidence links.

use_cases.title: Refresh Resume Accomplishments
use_cases.description: Convert verified contributions into resume material and remove confidential details intended only for internal documents.
use_cases.target_user: Developers updating resumes for job applications

prompt_templates.title: Start a Brag Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a brag document for my last six months of work. Ask me which repositories to use before collecting evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the review period and approved repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Review Local Contributions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use local Git history in [repository] for [author email] since [date]. Group contributions by theme and mark unknown results as gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: build a draft from a repository without GitHub collection.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Code and Team Contributions
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft my self-review for [date range] using only [approved repositories]. Restrict GitHub queries to those repositories. Include [mentoring and incident notes].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine repository evidence with work that Git cannot show.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Promotion Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a promotion outline from [approved evidence and notes]. Preserve team attribution, distinguish verified outcomes from gaps, and rank missing evidence. Ask three priority questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: refine contribution evidence into a promotion discussion.

output_examples.input: Sample evidence: PR #42 added retry handling on March 12. No outcome metrics were provided.
output: What I did: Added retry handling.
Result: [GAP: What changed for users or the team?]
Priority question: Do incident records show a change in failed requests after deployment?

output_examples.input: Sample notes: I owned the cache integration in a team project. User-provided measurements show response time fell from 240 ms to 180 ms.
output: What I did: Contributed the cache integration to a team performance project.
Result: User-provided measurements show response time decreased from 240 ms to 180 ms.
Scope signal: Owned the cache integration, not the entire project.
Evidence gap: Add the project link and measurement source.

best_practices: Agree on the time window and repository list, then add explicit repository filters before running GitHub searches.
Provide outcome measurements, evidence links, and notes about contributions that Git does not record.
Review attribution and remove confidential information before sharing the draft outside your organization.
anti_patterns: Treating commit counts or pull request titles as proof of business impact.
Claiming sole ownership of team results without evidence of your specific contribution.
Running an unrestricted account-wide search when only named repositories are approved.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub?
faq.answer: No. It includes a local Git log alternative filtered by author and start date.

faq.question: What happens when results are unknown?
faq.answer: The draft marks missing outcomes with visible gaps and ends with prioritized questions instead of inventing metrics.

faq.question: Can it include mentoring and incident work?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for user notes about mentoring, incidents, reviews, and other contributions that Git history may not capture.

faq.question: Will it search only the repositories I name?
faq.answer: The prose requires that boundary, but the example command lacks repository filters. Add explicit filters before running it.

faq.question: What formats can it produce?
faq.answer: It produces Markdown and offers to adapt the final document into a self-review, promotion packet outline, or resume bullets.
